# Final Review Proposal
**Producer:** agent:codex/gpt-5.4

## Summary

Reviewed the current worktree diff in `save.rs` and the shrimp-feeding changes. Two correctness issues remain: the legacy-save migration synthesizes reserve mass on load, and the new shrimp appetite cap still mixes biomass units with routing-mass units.

## Amendments

1. Do not seed `animal.reserve_g` from live shrimp counts in `crates/tank_core/src/save.rs:333-369`. `reserve_g` is a separate stored material pool, not the structural biomass already represented by `adults_count`/`juveniles_count`: it is counted independently in the elemental budgets (`crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:246-248`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:332-333`) and can be spent to create new shrimp biomass (`crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:639-657`). Reconstructing it from existing shrimp counts injects extra N/C into every migrated v3 save and can immediately fund hatching/maturation that the saved state never actually contained.
   Rationale: Legacy-save migration should preserve serialized mass, not create a new reserve pool on load.
2. Rework the new detritus-appetite cap in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:148-165` to use one consistent mass basis. `food_demand`/`periph_consumed` are raw periphyton biomass grams, but `detritus_consumed` and `daily_food_consumed_g` are organic-matter routing grams (`crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:86-89`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/budget.rs:379-385`). Because the remainder is computed as `food_demand - periph_consumed`, detritus-heavy diets can still overshoot the intended daily intake cap by roughly 4x at the default N:C ratio, and the added regression test at `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:835-871` currently encodes the same mixed-unit expectation.
   Rationale: The patch was meant to stop double-counting shrimp intake, but the new subtraction still applies the cap in mismatched units, so feeding/waste/reserve fluxes remain materially wrong.
